title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
abstract: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

bite.hook: New neural-network Gaussian tensor networks simulate strongly correlated fermions in lattices up to 1024 sites.
tldr: They introduced neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS) to simulate strongly correlated electrons.
They combined local Gaussian states with neural networks, achieving an exact contraction cost of O(N^(3/2)) on 2D lattices.
They obtained state-of-the-art variational energies for the Hubbard model at U/t=8 and 1/8 hole doping on lattices up to 1024 sites.
bite.whyItMatters: Simulating strongly correlated electrons is a major bottleneck in physics and materials science. This method provides a scalable way to model complex quantum systems accurately.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to predict how thousands of dancers move together when they are tightly packed and constantly bumping into each other. Researchers built a smarter math helper that combines artificial intelligence with special grid patterns to map these complex quantum movements easily.
